questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

All the buses leaving between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. __**has been cancelled.**__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**were cancelled**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this sentence, the subject is **'All the buses'. **
 
• Since it's a plural subject, we should use **'have' **instead of **'has'. **
 
• However, the sentence is referring to a past event - the cancellation of the buses.
 
• Therefore, instead of using a present tense verb, we should be using a past tense verb.
 
• The correct past tense conjugation in this case is **'were cancelled'.**
 
• Thus, the corrected sentence should read **"All the buses leaving between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. were cancelled."**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• were been cancelled:
 
 
• This option isn't correct because 'were been' is grammatically incorrect in English.
 
• It's not a proper use of verb tenses.
 
 
 
• being cancelled:
 
 
• This choice uses the passive continuous form which isn't accurate for a completed past action.
 
• The 'being' form should be used for ongoing actions in the past, which wouldn't be appropriate as the sentence refers to a completed action.

__
 
• The error lies in **option 2)** we have to change** 'the comforts to life' **into **'the comforts of life'** to make it grammatically correct.
 
• **Comforts of life** mean *the state of having a pleasant life with enough money for everything that we need.*
 
 
• ​**Example:** Deepshikha's mother Vindhyanjali forgot her **comforts of life** for the overall development of Deepshikha and her brother Gyaneshwan.
 
 

Hence, **option 2) the comforts to life **contains an error.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Most lizards rely on camouflage to hide from their enemies.

options.text: Camouflage has been relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.
Camouflage is relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.
Camouflage was relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.
Most lizards are being relied on by camouflage to hide from their enemies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Camouflage is relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the passive voice, the *subject__ is __acted upon__ by the __verb__.*

 __
 
• Example: Kho-kho is liked by Upasana.
 
 
 
• In the active voice, the *subject__ __performs__ an __action__.*
 
 
• Example: Upasana likes kho-kho.
 
 
 
• The formula used for a present active voice is:
 
 
• Subject (Most lizards) + V1 (rely on) + Object (Camouflage) + Remaining Sentence (if any).
 
 
 
• So, we know that the sentence is in the present active voice so for changing the present active voice into the present passive voice. The formula used will be :
 
 
• Object (Camouflage) + is/am/are + V3 (relied on) + by + Subject (most lizards) + Remaining Sentence (if any).
 
 

Hence, **option 2) Camouflage is relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. It coincided with the 140th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

B. Through this innovative measure, the knowledge of the traditions and culture of different states is being shared.

C. The initiative ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’ was launched by the Honourable Prime Minister on 31st October 2015.

D. This will lead to an enhanced bonding and national integration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**CABD**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In order to find out the correct order of the given sentences, we need to establish a connection between the sentences.
 
• We will first use the statement 'C' as it is given us an introduction about the topic i.e. the launch of the '**Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat**' initiative on 31st October 2015 .
 
• It will be followed by the statement 'A' as it is further telling us about that on the same date, 140th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was observed.
 
• Next, we will use the statement 'B' as it is conveying the sharing of knowledge of traditions through the innovative measure.
 
• Finally, we will conclude with statement 'D'.
 
• Hence, option 4 'CABD' is the correct answer.

So the complete passage is- ***C.** The initiative ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’ was launched by the Honourable Prime Minister on 31st October 2015. **A.** It coincided with the 140th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. **B.** Through this innovative measure, the knowledge of the traditions and culture of different states is being shared. **D.** This will lead to an enhanced bonding and national integration.*

**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

The increase in irrigated areas /has resulted on achieving / record food grain production.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**has resulted on achieving**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the error is in the usage of **prepositions**.
 
• A **preposition** is a word or group of words used before a noun, pronoun, or noun phrase to show direction, time, place, location, spatial relationships, etc.
 
 
• **​For eg.-** in the box, on the ceiling, on earth, in India, etc.
 
 
 
• With **achieving** we will use the preposition '**in**' instead of '**on**'.
 
• Hence, **option 2** is the correct answer.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *The increase in irrigated areas has resulted **in **achieving record food grain production.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In the given sentence, the verb '**has resulted**' agrees with the subject '**The increase**'.
 
• Hence, '**has**' has been used and not '**have**'.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

They cried, “Bravo! Well done.”

options.text: They shouted in joy that they had done well.
They cried in joy for doing well.
They cried loudly for doing well.
They exclaimed with wonder that they had done well.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**They shouted in joy that they had done well.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given is an exclamatory sentence
 
• The following rules are to be kept in mind while converting a declarative sentence to an indirect sentence:
 
 
• 'cried' will be changed to 'shouted in joy' as it can be observed that the sentence is of joy..
 
• Pronoun '**they**' will be used to refer to the people being talked about.
 
• Modal 'had' will be used to denote the past perfect tense.
 
• The exclamation '**Bravo!**' will be removed.
 
• To remove the inverted commas and the comma, we will use 'that'.
 
 
 
• Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

*The correct sentence is:* They shouted in joy that they had done well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bravo** is used to express approval when a performer or other person has done something well.

 
• **For eg.-** Bravo, you're improving!
